subject: FintechCo multi-region performance & competitive follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@fintechco.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: multi-region perf & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Main priorities you shared:
- Low p99 latency across US + EU for customer-facing scoring pipeline (~200ms target)
- Data residency for EU transactions (log retention, KV cache residency)
- Predictable cost compared to hyperscaler endpoints (we discussed both $/token and per-request overhead)

2) What we (Redwood) will deliver for the next test: 
- Short benchmark comparing Redwood hosted endpoints vs one hyperscaler-managed endpoint across 3 regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) using your representative payload and seq lengths.
- A proposed multi-region MVP plan that shows routing, cache residency options, and failover.
- Latency workbook and test harness so you can reproduce.

3) Proposed next steps / timeline: 
- Redwood to run initial perf tests and share workbook by Mon (7/20). -> Deliverable: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-latency.xlsx
- Joint test window: Wed 7/22 to validate in your staging tenants (we need one contact + IP allowlist).
- Legal / procurement: we flagged potential contract windows; Marissa will sync separately on pricing/terms.

Questions for you: can you confirm the staging cluster region(s) you want us to target for the joint run? Also who should be the contact for IP/network whitelist?

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com]
[Attachment: MVP plan stub (mvp-multi-region-plan.pdf)]

From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@fintechco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: multi-region perf & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the concise recap. A few quick answers: 

- Target staging regions: us-east (primary), eu-west (for EU residency testing). We can spin up a small staging cluster in ap-south later but not needed for the initial run.
- Whitelist contact: Priya (cc'd) will handle the network config and can provide the IPs.

One ask on the benchmark: please include both steady-state throughput (tokens/s) and p50/p95/p99 latency under our 3 seq-length payloads. Also flag any cases where quantization or batching materially changes quality vs baseline. We had a previous incident where a quantized variant introduced a tokenization mismatch — want to avoid surprises.

Alex
Alex Smith
Head of ML Infrastructure, FintechCo
alex.smith@fintechco.com

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: multi-region perf & next steps

Alex — great, thanks for confirming. We'll include the p50/p95/p99 buckets and throughput metrics in the workbook. A few clarifications on our side: 

- Test harness: we'll run 1) Redwood hosted endpoint (nearest region routing) 2) Hyperscaler managed inference endpoint (same model size) with identical request shaping. For fairness we'll disable cross-request caching in the hyperscaler run and enable our controlled prefix/KV caching in Redwood runs as a separate series.
- Quantization/quality: we'll run full-precision and int8-style quantized variants and include a short QA diff (BLEU/embedding-similarity checks) against your golden set.
- Data residency: for EU tests we'll demonstrate KV cache residency options (cache-in-region vs global) and outline trade-offs in the MVP doc.

Deliverables by EOD Mon (7/20): latency workbook (xlsx), short notes on config used, and a proposed joint test window slot for Wed 7/22.

For the joint run we'll need:
- Priya's whitelist IPs (or a temporary allowlist we can use)
- A sampling of ~100 representative requests across your three seq-lengths (you can drop a CSV in the Drive link)

Thanks — looping Sean and Marissa to coordinate procurement & pricing.

Jordan

Alex / Priya —

Thanks — quick note from procurement/solutions: 

- Attached is the initial latency workbook (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-latency.xlsx) and a one-pager MVP plan (mvp-multi-region-plan.pdf). The workbook has three tabs: config, raw-runs, and summary charts. We included both FP16 and int8-style quant runs.
- Based on the initial runs, high-level takeaways: Redwood hosted endpoints show ~25-35ms lower p99 in us-west/us-east for your mid-length payload when our cache-in-region is enabled. Hyperscaler endpoint had lower cold-start overhead in eu-west but higher sustained p99 under load. We'll annotate the workbook with the exact run configs.
- Next tests: Jordan proposed Wed 7/22 for a joint run in your staging. Priya, can you confirm a 2-hour window and drop the whitelist IPs? Also please upload the representative CSV to the Drive link above.

Attachments: [redwood-vs-hyperscaler-latency.xlsx] [mvp-multi-region-plan.pdf]

Regards,
